summary: Fremont County peak where a 1965 Pinedale Roundup interview, as quoted by Kemnow, has Charlie Bayer using it as a fire lookout from 1910; FFLA lists it as undocumented.

events.note: Charlie Bayer's own recollection, as quoted from a 1965 interview: he used the mountain as a fire lookout beginning in 1910. No agency or register record is cited for this.

evidence.supports: interview with Charlie Bayer printed in The Pinedale Roundup, dated October 7, 1965
evidence.quote: October 7, 1965: From an interview with Charlie Bayer in The Pinedale Roundup

evidence.supports: Bayer used the mountain as a fire lookout from 1910 and climbed to its top during fire season; the quoted words mention no structure
evidence.quote: beginning in 1910 I used it as a fire lookout, climbing to its top frequently and regularly during fire season.

evidence.supports: location one mile east of Middle Fork Station, between Big Popo Agie and Sawmill Creek canyons
evidence.quote: Bayer Mountain is one mile east of the Middle Fork Station between Big Popo Agie and Sawmill Creek Canyons.

evidence.supports: Kemnow's site gives Bayer Mountain its own page among its forest lookouts
Bayer Mountain is in the association's unknown or undocumented group
Bayer Mountain listed in Fremont County in that group
a site moves to the lookout lists if evidence or documentation shows regular fire-lookout use
evidence.quote: If evidence or documentation is uncovered showing that any of these were actually used as regular wildland fire lookout sites, they will be moved to the lookout lists.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Kemnow's site gives Bayer Mountain its own page among forest lookouts and quotes Bayer's use from 1910. The association lists the site as unknown or undocumented and moves sites to its lookout lists when evidence of regular use turns up. The story reports both views and does not decide between them.

notes_for_editor: Two sources, both thin. The 1910 use and the 1965 interview come only from Kemnow's page, which quotes The Pinedale Roundup, dated October 7, 1965; the newspaper itself was not read, and the quote is Bayer's own recollection. The quoted words describe climbing to the top and mention no structure, so the story does not say a lookout building stood there. The association lists the site as undocumented and gives no coordinates for it. The record's coordinates (42.6419, -108.8304) are attributed to west_us_lookouts, but the page text read here has no coordinates, so they were not verified. No source found describes a structure, a removal, or current access. The story body is 165 words, within range.
